Summary

Fixes the four P1 bugs in milestone 7 ("Scaffolder: honest recap"). In each case, any reported a parameter or a type as inferred even though the generated file was wrong. Each fix makes the refusal explicit without introducing new inference rules (ADR-0046).

Type of change

  • Bug fix
  • New feature
  • Breaking change
  • Refactoring
  • Analyzer / diagnostic change
  • Tests
  • Documentation
  • Build / CI / tooling

Changes

  • Guards below the first state write (any: Guards after the first state write are neither read nor flagged for review #297). The guard reader used to stop at the first assignment to state. It still does not read anything past that point, but it now keeps walking the body. A statement there that throws, or a call the closed set recognises as a guard, marks every parameter it would have constrained as unread guards, so the blocking line from ADR-0083 is emitted. A null-check there stays silent. An unrecognised call such as _items.AddRange(items) also stays silent; otherwise constructors with no guard at all would be blocked. This remaining gap is now documented in spec §9.
  • Indirect guards through a local or a member (any: Indirect guards are missed while the summary claims they were inferred #300, any: Guards after the first state write are neither read nor flagged for review #297). A throwing statement now follows each local it tests back to that local's declaration, and each field or property it tests back to the earlier assignments of it in the same body (one step only). It marks the parameters named on the right side. The guard itself is still not read.
    • A null-check stays silent only on a member holding the parameter itself (allowing parentheses, a built-in cast or !).
    • A null-check on a value computed from the parameter is marked. That covers name.Length < 5 ? null : name, a helper returning null, and a user-defined conversion, whether written as a cast ((ProductCode)raw) or applied implicitly (Code = raw;).
    • The 16 delegate-computed-* sweep cases are reclassified from KnownResidue to BlockedForVerification, and sweep-baseline.tsv is updated accordingly.
  • Self-referencing types (any scaffolds self-referencing types into unbounded recursion #299). A parameter that refers to the type being scaffolded is left open instead of being composed into new AnyNode() inside AnyNode itself. This applies to direct references and references through nullable types, arrays, or generic type arguments. The parameter gets the new Provenance.SelfReferencing, the recap label self-referencing, and a TODO line explaining why. Mutual recursion between two types through their own generators is not detected; the spec says so, and any: two types that reach each other scaffold into a stack overflow #332 tracks it.
  • Enums (any generate <Enum> reports success but emits return new TEnum() #298). An enum target is now refused with a new ScaffoldStatus.TypeIsEnum: exit code 1, nothing written, and a message pointing to Any.Enum<TEnum>(). The maintainer chose refusal over delegation.
  • Refactor. A behaviour-preserving extraction that keeps Guards.Read, the below-the-scan marking and Scaffolder.Scaffold within Sonar's S3776/S3267 limits.
  • Two existing tests asserted the old silent behaviour. They now assert the mark: AThrowingCheckAfterTheFirstAssignmentIsNotAGuard and AnUnrecognisedAssignmentStillEndsTheScan.
  • JustDummies.Cli/CHANGELOG.md has one Fixed entry per issue.
  • The review's wording fixes (EN/FR specification, French any page, the Composed XML summary) are folded into the commits they belong to. The last four commits come from the review:
    • the field-copy guard and its null-check exemption;
    • the restriction of that exemption to plain copies;
    • the exclusion of user-defined conversions, explicit;
    • the exclusion of user-defined conversions, implicit.
  • Not in this PR, both predating it, both judged non-blocking by the maintainer and tracked in [Needs a decision] any: mark every visible throw unless proven harmless, instead of listing the shapes that earn a mark #333:
    • a null-check through an overloaded ==;
    • a copy into a property whose custom set accessor transforms the value.

Testing

  • dotnet build JustDummies.sln — no warnings left in JustDummies.GenAny or JustDummies.Cli.

  • dotnet test --solution JustDummies.sln — not run as a whole. On the final head I ran JustDummies.GenAny.UnitTests (737 passed), JustDummies.Cli.UnitTests (126 passed) and JustDummies.Documentation.UnitTests (11 passed). The core, analyzer and xUnit suites were not run; their code is unchanged.

  • Analyzer tests pass (JustDummies.Analyzers.UnitTests) — not run; no analyzer change.

  • Full generative sweep (JUSTDUMMIES_SWEEP=1): passed with the updated baseline on the final head.

  • Red before green. The any scaffolds self-referencing types into unbounded recursion #299 and any generate <Enum> reports success but emits return new TEnum() #298 assertions, rewritten without the new symbols, fail on origin/main on the symptom itself (7/7):

    • any scaffolds self-referencing types into unbounded recursion #299: new AnyNode(), Any.ListOf(new AnyNode()), Any.ArrayOf(new AnyNode());
    • any generate <Enum> reports success but emits return new TEnum() #298: both enums come back Scaffolded.

    They pass on the branch. The tests for the three review fixes (computed member, explicit and implicit user-defined conversion) were written first: red on the previous head on the UnreadGuards assertion, green after the fix.

  • The UX trial's Bug_ tests (tools/ux-trial, on commit d32c8dc) are not on main, so they were neither run nor retired here.

Documentation

  • Public API / analyzer documentation updated
  • README / doc/ updated — any specification §5.1, §5.3, §5.4, §6, §7, §9; the justdummies-cli user page; the genany-sweep workflow page.
  • French translation updated alongside the English page it mirrors (every page above has its .fr twin updated)
  • No documentation change required

Architecture decisions

  • No architectural decision in this pull request
  • New decision recorded — ADR drafted as Proposed: ADR-____
  • Supersedes an existing ADR — successor proposed, status not flipped: ADR-____
  • ⚠️ Conflicts with an existing ADR — flagged for the maintainer: ADR-0089

⚠️ Conflicts with ADR-0089 (Draw a composed parameter through the generator its type owns). The decision says a composed parameter is drawn through new Any{T}(), and spec §5.4 says "the parameter is never left unresolved for a composed type". #299 introduces one exception: when T is the type being scaffolded, the parameter is left open as self-referencing, because new AnyT() inside AnyT's own constructor recurses as soon as it is constructed. This is the narrowest fix the issue asked for. Whether the exception deserves an amendment or a successor ADR is your call. Note also that #297 removes the spec's former statement that "past the first assignment, a throwing if is ordinary logic"; this follows from ADR-0083 and is recorded in §5.3.

Related issues

Closes #297
Closes #298
Closes #299
Closes #300

Follow-ups: #332 (mutual recursion between two scaffolded types), #333 (null-check exemptions proven rather than syntactic: an overloaded ==, a property with a custom setter).

Contributor agreement

  • I have read the Contributor Agreement and, if I am not the Project Owner (@Reefact), I accept it for this contribution.

issue (blocking): Une vérification de null sur un champ bloque le build

[P2] Le suivi ajouté par ReachedThroughACopy marque systématiquement le paramètre, avant de distinguer une garde qui impose réellement une contrainte. Exemple :

public Subject(string name) {
    Name = name;
    if (Name is null) { throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(name)); }
}
public string Name { get; }

Après Name = name, le parcours passe par ReadChain puis ReadOne. Mentioned ne trouve aucun paramètre dans Name is null, mais ReachedThroughACopy retrouve name dans l'affectation et appelle MarkUnread. Le générateur Any.String().NonEmpty() ne tire pourtant jamais null : ce constructeur n'a aucune contrainte non satisfaite et son fichier généré ne devrait pas être bloqué. Le test existant AStatementAfterTheFirstAssignmentThatWouldNarrowNothingMarksNothing vérifie déjà ce comportement pour if (name is null), mais pas pour la propriété copiée.

Merci d'ajouter cette variante au test et de préserver le traitement silencieux des vérifications déjà garanties par le générateur, y compris lorsqu'elles utilisent un champ ou une propriété copiés.

Confirmed by running the CLI packed from d265f9c. The over-marking is real, and the PR introduces it:

Constructor body Recap
Name = name; if (Name is null) throw … to verify, unread guards
_name = name; if (_name == null) throw … to verify, unread guards
_name = name; ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(_name); inferred, silent
Name = name; if (name is null) throw … inferred, silent

So the helper spelling and the direct check are already treated as satisfied by construction, and only the if form through a copy is not. Running the copy-followed parameters through the same "would this narrow anything" test that MarkIfItRejectsBelowTheScan applies before marking, instead of marking them unconditionally, should close it. The two if rows belong in AStatementAfterTheFirstAssignmentThatWouldNarrowNothingMarksNothing.

Resolved in d22ec04. ReadOne no longer follows a copy when the condition is a null-check (x is null, x == null, null == x): the generator never draws null (ADR-0064), so the member it was copied into cannot be null either. Name is null, Name == null and ThrowIfNull(Name) are now rows of AStatementAfterTheFirstAssignmentThatWouldNarrowNothingMarksNothing. With the fix disabled, the two if rows fail; with it, 728/728 pass. The field-copy tests still mark.

its declaration and marks the parameters the initializer names as
unread guards. It never reads such a guard: following the value further
would be propagation, which ADR-0046 refuses.

The sixteen delegate-computed sweep shapes leave the known residue for
BlockedForVerification; the baseline moves with them, and spec §9 and
the user page now name the shapes that still escape.

Roslyn synthesises a parameterless constructor for an enum, and the
implicit-constructor exclusion only covered structs, so the scaffolder
emitted `return new TEnum();` and exited 0. Every draw was (TEnum)0: a
constant, or an undeclared value when the enum has no zero member.

after the generic check: exit 1, nothing written, and a sentence naming
Any.Enum<TEnum>(), which the library already draws it with. Spec §5.1
and §7 record the refusal and its place in the order.
